extracted.intended_audience: broadcasters, comedy writers and producers, industry press, and general audiences interested in TV commissioning
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and signals about what kinds of half-hour, post-watershed scripted comedies Sky and FX seek to co-develop and co-fund — including format, tone, talent and channel-fit considerations for productions aimed at both UK/Ireland and US audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive brand new comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Create 'distinctive brand new comedy' — original comedy concepts rather than reboots or adaptations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreement is to 'co-develop distinctive brand new comedy' and to 'create brand new post-watershed comedy' that is original and sits alongside Sky and FX's existing original series. Emphasis on originality and distinctiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-watershed content
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows should be suitable for the post-watershed broadcast window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deal specifically targets 'post-watershed comedy', indicating content can be oriented toward adult audiences and themes appropriate for late-night scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format: half-hour scripted comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: The projects targeted are half-hour, scripted comedy series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-year agreement will see Sky and FX co-develop 'new half-hour scripted comedy.' This is an explicit format constraint for projects under this partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-funding and co-development model
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are to be co-funded and co-developed by Sky and FX Networks under the partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The partners 'co-fund and co-develop' projects; if commissioned, shows would be broadcast on Sky channels in the UK/Ireland and FX channels in the US. Submission/creation should expect collaborative development and shared financing/notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel and broadcast fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedies should be appropriate for Sky1 HD or Sky Atlantic HD (UK/Ireland) and FX Networks channels (US).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press release states commissioned shows would air on Sky1 HD or Sky Atlantic HD in the UK/Ireland and on FX Networks channels in the US — projects should fit those channels' tone, standards and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Atlantic appeal / 'bridge the Atlantic'
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows should be able to entertain audiences in both the UK and the US — have cross-Atlantic storytelling or appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eric Schrier: partnership aims to 'create comedies that will bridge the Atlantic and entertain audiences in both the UK and US.' Development should consider themes, humor and sensibilities that translate across both markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talent: involve top on- and off-screen talent from UK and US
rubrics_metrics.description: Development should involve high-caliber writers, performers and production personnel from both Britain and the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deal 'will involve the very best on- and off-screen talent from both Britain and the US.' Emphasis on securing strong creative teams and recognizable or high-quality creative talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone/style alignment with exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedies should align stylistically or tonally with the kinds of shows Sky and FX currently champion (e.g., A Touch of Cloth, Alan Partridge’s Mid-Morning Matters, Louie, It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release cites specific series as comparable: Sky's A Touch of Cloth and Alan Partridge’s Mid-Morning Matters, and FX's Louie and It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia. Use these as exemplars for the desired tone, distinctiveness and edge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home-grown / original British production emphasis (for Sky)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sky emphasizes commitment to original home-grown British programming and substantial investment in UK production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sky highlights being 'the UK's biggest investor in television content' and will 'invest £600 million in original British production' this year — projects that contribute to Sky's home-grown slate are desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and award-calibre expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are expected to be of high quality with potential for critical acclaim and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release references 'distinctive, award-winning comedy' and lists past commissions that have earned Emmys, BAFTAs and other awards; implies a preference for projects with strong creative ambition and award potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with networks' existing comedy development slates
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should be compatible with FX's active comedy development and programming expansion and Sky's comedy commissioning strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FX's 2014 slate and active development of pilots (listed in the release) show what kinds of scripted comedy FX is developing: adult, sometimes edgy comedies (including animation and single-camera fare). Alignment with each network's commissioning trends increases likelihood of consideration.
